decisions.latin: Confitébor tibi, Dómine, in toto corde meo
decisions.why: D5: *confitéri* said to God is *dar graças a*. The whole first colon is 9:2a word for word in the Latin (and 137:1), so it copies 9:2's Portuguese exactly: *Eu vos darei graças, Senhor, de todo o meu coração* (*in toto corde → de todo o coração*, the formula row). This is the opening of a Sunday Vespers psalm; the Brazilian Lectionary's stanza (CNBB, from the Hebrew; fetched, see liturgy-br.txt) begins *Eu agradeço a Deus de todo o coração* — the same verb family and the same *de todo o coração*, so the ear that knows the Mass psalm is not surprised. *Louvar* is refused under D5 (it is *laudáre*'s word; 110:10b *laudátio* in this psalm).

options.label: Eu vos darei graças
options.note: Ruling: D5; = 9:2 word for word.

options.label: Eu vos louvarei
options.note: MS1932 *Louvar-te-ei*, DRB *I will praise thee*; refused under D5 (collides with *laudátio → louvor* in 110:10b).

options.label: Eu vos confessarei
options.note: the cognate; refused under D5 (heard as professing faith, or opaque).

decisions.why: The Latin names the just once and leaves *congregatióne* bare: whose congregation is not said (the Greek is the same, ἐν βουλῇ εὐθείων καὶ συναγωγῇ). Kept open, in the Latin's order, *congregação* by the *congregátio* row (61:9) and *conselho* by D33 (which names 110:1 as a deliberating body). MS1932 (*no conselho e na assembleia dos justos*) and DM1962 (from the Hebrew) move *dos justos* to govern both — that closes what the Latin leaves open, and spends *assembleia*, which is *ecclésia*'s (D34). **Readers (v1):** the stylist heard *coração / congregação* as a loud rhyme and *congregação* as bureaucratic, and asked *e na assembleia*: refused — *assembleia* is *ecclésia*'s (D34), and the rhyme is the price of two rulings (the 9:2a formula and the row); kept as an option. The ambiguity reader heard *conselho* first as advice — D33 keeps *conselho* where the Latin can mean both; accepted.

decisions.why: *Exquisíta* is the participle of *exquírere* ('sought out'; L&S also 'carefully devised, choice'); the Greek ἐξεζητημένα is the same. The glossary gives *exquírere → procurar* (Ps 118, 13:2), so the participle keeps the row: *procuradas*. *In omnes voluntátes ejus* (εἰς πάντα τὰ θελήματα αὐτοῦ): *in* + accusative, 'unto / according to all his wills' — DRB *according to*; the *ejus* is the Lord's (singular). *Segundo* is DRB's reading and the least forced Portuguese; it leaves open whether the works are sought out by men or wrought to suit God's wills, as the Latin does. The Hebrew's 'studied by all who delight in them' (DM1962 *contempladas por todos os que as amam*) is not followed (rule 1). The cognate *exquisitas* is 'odd' in Brazil and is refused. **Draft 2:** the Latinist (v1, minor) found that *segundo* settles the open *in* + accusative on "according to", and asked for bare *em*; taken — the Latin leaves open whether the works are sought out in, for, or according to all his wills, and *em* keeps that. The stylist called the colon the worst line (*procuradas* heard as "in demand", the colon hard to parse) and asked *primorosas segundo*: refused and kept as an option — *primorosas* takes the adjectival sense of the participle ("choice, exquisite", which L&S does give) and drops the seeking that the Latin and the Greek ἐξεζητημένα both carry, and *segundo* is the closing the Latinist refused. The ambiguity reader heard the colon as vague — the Latin is.

options.note: *buscar* is *quǽrere*'s verb; refused for the row.

decisions.why: The noun *conféssio* is left open by D5; its twins 95:6 (*Conféssio, et pulchritúdo*) and 103:1b (*Confessiónem, et decórem*) both ruled *confissão* — the Latin's word and its range (praise confessed; for some readers sin confessed), and the noun of the verb that opens this very psalm (ἐξομολογέομαι / ἐξομολόγησις). Followed, so that the three attribute-pairs read alike. *Magnificéntia → magnificência* (row; 95:6 has it too). Order: the Latin puts the predicate first and has no verb; the copula is supplied (D2) and the Latin's order kept, so that the line begins, like 95:6, on *Confissão*. The cost, as at 95:6: *confissão* is heard first as the sacrament. MS1932 *A sua obra é glória e magnificência* and the Lectionary *Que beleza e esplendor são os seus feitos* go their own ways. **Readers (v1):** the stylist asked *Louvor* (the sense is praise) and the ambiguity reader heard the sacrament first — the cost already named at 95:6 and 103:1b. Refused for those rulings and for *laudátio → louvor* in 110:10b; Gustavo decides the three twins together.

decisions.why: The Latin's noun and light verb: *memóriam fecit* (μνείαν ἐποιήσατο). *Fez memória de* is living Brazilian church speech ('to make memory of, commemorate'), keeps both words and leaves open, as the Latin does, whether he himself remembers or leaves a remembrance to men. *memória* is the row's word (29:5, 96:12); *memorial* is *memoriále*'s (101:13) and is kept apart. *mirabília → maravilhas* (9:2 and passim). The Lectionary has *nos deixou a lembrança de suas grandes maravilhas*.

decisions.why: The pair of 85:15 and 102:8 (*miserátor → compassivo*, *miséricors → misericordioso*, the row), here in the other order, which is kept: *misericordioso e compassivo*. The Latin has no verb; DRB reads the words as in apposition to the subject of *fecit* ('being a merciful and gracious Lord'), and so does the ruling: *o Senhor misericordioso e compassivo* names the subject of *Fez memória* and *deu alimento* without supplying anything. 102:8's build (*Compassivo e misericordioso é o Senhor*) stands alone there, where there is no verb to hang the subject on; here the copula would make the middle colon a sentence of its own and cut the subject from both verbs.

decisions.latin: Memor erit in sǽculum testaménti sui
decisions.why: *memor esse* → *lembrar-se de* (row); *in sǽculum → para sempre* (D23); *testaméntum → aliança* (row). The subject is named with proclisis, as the row did at 86:4 (*Eu me lembrarei*), to avoid the mesóclise *Lembrar-se-á* at the head of a verse; the future is the Latin's (*erit*; the Lectionary's refrain *O Senhor se lembra sempre da aliança* is a present from the Hebrew). 104:8 (*Memor fuit in sǽculum testaménti sui*, being translated in parallel) should read *Lembrou-se para sempre da sua aliança* in the same words, past for past.

options.label: Lembrar-se-á

decisions.why: *mandáre* with a thing as object is *ordenar* in the finished psalms (32:9 *ele ordenou*, 43:5 *que ordenais as salvações de Jacó*, and 104:8 in draft *da palavra que ordenou*). *Mandou* would keep the echo of 110:8 *mandáta → mandamentos*, but in Brazil *mandar* + a thing is heard first as 'sent' — and it would stand beside *Enviou* in the same verse, making two sendings of one. *in ætérnum → para sempre* (D23). MS1932 and DM1962 *estabeleceu* interpret.

decisions.why: Two questions. (1) The word: the *inítium* row gives *início* (kept apart from *princípium → princípio*, 118:152/160). Here it departs from the row: *O temor do Senhor é o princípio da sabedoria* is one of the best-known lines of Scripture in Portuguese — MS1932 and DM1962 (parallels file) both have exactly these words, as do the Almeida Bibles for Ps 111:10 (fetched, liturgy-br.txt) — and this psalm has no *princípium* to be kept apart from; ἀρχή is the Greek of both Latin words, so D15's test allows it (77:2 *ab inítio → desde o princípio* already departs from the row). (2) The order: the Latin is verbless with the predicate first; the copula is supplied and the subject put first (D2: natural order), which is also the order every Portuguese witness has and ends the colon on *sabedoria*, where the Latin's *Dómini* is replaced by a paroxytone.

decisions.why: Verbless, with a dative of possession: 'good understanding [is] to all who do it'. *têm* is supplied, the plainest Portuguese for the dative of possession (grammar, D2). *intelléctus → entendimento* (row, 31:8–9). *eum* is masculine in the Latin (the Greek has αὐτήν, wisdom): it can refer to *timor* or to *intelléctus*; Portuguese *o* is masculine too and keeps both open. *fácere* → *praticar*: *fazer o temor* is not Portuguese; *praticar* is *operári*'s verb elsewhere, but *operári* is not in this psalm (DM1962 *os que o praticam*, from the Hebrew, for rhythm only). MS1932 *São sábios todos aqueles que procedem segundo este temor* glosses. **Ambiguity reader (v1):** *os que o praticam* has an unclear antecedent (fear, wisdom, commandments) — the Latin's *eum* is as open, and is kept so; *Bom entendimento* was heard with "a real chance" of "getting along well" — the row's word (31:8–9) is kept, *inteligência* (MS1932, DM1962 elsewhere) would take *intellígere*'s family.

choices.110:1: Soft flag accepted: *coração / congregação* rhyme at mediant and final, which the Latin (*meo / congregatióne*) does not have. Both words are fixed by rulings — the first colon copies 9:2a (D5 formula), *congregação* is the *congregátio* row — and the only escapes are to reorder the Latin's two nouns or to spend *assembleia* (*ecclésia*'s, D34). Left for the stylist's ear.
choices.110:2: *Grandes são as obras do Senhor*: copula supplied (D2); MS1932 word for word. *voluntátes* plural kept (*vontades*, as 15:3 *todas as minhas vontades*). Draft 2: *segundo* → *em* (Latinist; decision `exquisita`).
choices.110:3: The second colon *e a sua justiça permanece pelos séculos dos séculos* is repeated in 110:10b with *o seu louvor*, as the Latin repeats *manet in sǽculum sǽculi*; *pelos séculos dos séculos* (D27) ends on a proparoxytone, as *sǽculi* does.
choices.110:4: *escam dedit timéntibus se → deu alimento aos que o temem*: *esca* given → *alimento* (the *esca* row; 103:27); MS1932 word for word.
choices.110:5b: *virtútem óperum suórum annuntiábit pópulo suo* → *anunciará ao seu povo o poder das suas obras*: *annuntiáre → anunciar* (D41), *virtus → poder* (row); the Latin's future kept (the Greek's aorist ἀνήγγειλεν is not followed, rule 1); natural order puts the indirect object first. The verse ends in a colon, as the Latin does, because 110:7 continues it.
choices.110:7: *Ut det illis → Para lhes dar* (purpose; proclisis after *para*). *véritas, et judícium → verdade e juízo*: the rows (*juízo*, not the Lectionary's *justiça*, which is *justítia*'s, 110:3). Copula supplied.
choices.110:8: *Fidélia → Fiéis são* (copula supplied, the Latin's order); *confirmáta → confirmados* (the *confirmáre* row: with things as object the cognate is right; the Lectionary has *confirmados* too); *in veritáte et æquitáte → em verdade e equidade*, no articles, as the Latin (*equidade* is the row's word, noted unknown by some readers; kept). The mediant falls on *séculos* (proparoxytone), as the Latin's *sǽculi*: the formula is not bent for the cadence.
choices.110:9a: *Redemptiónem → redenção* (the *redímere* row: the noun keeps the Christian word), without an article as the Latin; MS1932 *a redenção*. *misit → Enviou*.
choices.110:9b: *Sanctum, et terríbile nomen ejus → Santo e terrível é o seu nome*: *terríbilis → terrível* (D43; the row names 110:9), the Latin's order, copula supplied; MS1932 word for word. The ambiguity reader heard *terrível* partly as "horrible" and *temor* as being afraid of God — both the rows' known costs (D43; *timor → temor*), kept.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps110.md (Latin, LXX, Hebrew, DRB, MS1932, DM1962). Rows applied: D5 *dar graças* (110:1 copies 9:2a), D33 *conselho*, *congregátio → congregação*, *exquírere → procurar*, *conféssio → confissão* (95:6, 103:1b), *magnificência*, *miséricors / miserátor* (85:15, 102:8), *memor esse*, D23, *testaméntum → aliança*, D41, *virtus → poder*, *juízo*, *mandáta → mandamentos*, *equidade*, *redenção*, *mandáre → ordenar* (32:9, 43:5), D43 *terrível*, *intelléctus → entendimento*, D27 *pelos séculos dos séculos*, the *(fit reverentia)* row. Departure: *inítium → princípio* in the known line (decision `initium`). Brazilian liturgical circulation checked (liturgy-br.txt): the CNBB Lectionary's psalm 110(111) — *Eu agradeço a Deus de todo o coração*, refrain *O Senhor se lembra sempre da aliança* — is from the Hebrew and paraphrastic; used only to confirm that *dar graças … de todo o coração*, *alimento aos que o temem* and *confirmados* are what the ear knows. The CNBB Liturgia das Horas page could not be fetched.

Hard checks pass (ids 110:1–10b, every † and *). Soft flags, all accepted: 110:1 rhyme *coração / congregação* (see choices); 110:3b and 110:10b the formula *pelos séculos dos séculos* (+4, +2); 110:4 first colon −3 and middle colon +3 (they balance; the pair of adjectives is fixed by the row); 110:5b first colon +3 (the subject named, D2); 110:9b second colon +3 (the known line, decision `initium`).
One minor; taken. Tenses, persons, supplied copulas and pointing all passed.
